$Comment: Tools, paid out by Trim Work. A sawyer wears a hatchet down, so the yard keeps them in
gear: a spare hatchet now and then, and repair kits more often than that.
BOTH ROLLS READ WOODCUTTING LEVEL ALONE, deliberately. The wage table pays on level and luck
together, which rewards investment; this one is about where the worker is in their trade, so a
luck-heavy build gets the same spanner as anyone else at that level.
EACH ROLL PAIRS A CHANCE WITH A LADDER, which is what keeps this two rolls rather than six. The
Chance decides whether anything is handed over at all; the Ladder then decides WHICH tier, and
because floors are highest-wins and not cumulative, exactly one item comes out of each roll. A
worker at level ninety gets the top tier and nothing else, never one of each.
BOTH LADDERS START AT ZERO on purpose, below the level the quest that opens Trim Work asks for.
A ladder grants NOTHING when every floor sits above the worker's reading, so the bottom rung is
what keeps a roll that fired from handing over an empty hand if a level ever comes in lower than
the quest's gate implies. Keep it when you re-tune the rungs above it.
THE HATCHET LADDER STOPS AT COBALT on purpose. The questline Trim Work sits beside ends with a
cobalt-headed hatchet carrying stats no vanilla tool has, so a hatchet handed out here must never
reach past it. Raise a floor if you want a tier to arrive later; do not add a rung above cobalt.
The top rung is a plain vanilla cobalt hatchet, so be clear about what it does and does not
match: it cuts exactly as fast as the questline's own and shares its quality and item level,
while the questline's keeps the longer wear and the three stat channels to itself. A worker who
already carries that one is being handed a spare here, not a rival to it.
Repair kits come on roughly one run in eight, against a hatchet at about one run in twenty,
because a kit is upkeep and a hatchet is a small event. Only the hatchet roll carries a Cue: a
repair kit lands too often to make each one feel special, and a chime for it would cheapen the
ones that matter.
Name: Mmo_Sawmill_Trim_Supply

Rolls.$Comment: A spare hatchet, at the tier the worker's level has earned.

Floors.$Comment: The safety net, under the level the quest that opens Trim Work asks for. A ladder grants nothing when every floor sits above the worker, so this rung is what keeps the roll honest for anyone who arrives lower than expected.

Rolls.$Comment: Repair kits, the everyday upkeep, at the tier the worker's level has earned.

Floors.$Comment: The crude kit covers everything below the iron rung, starting at zero so the roll always has a floor to land on.
